papers.title: Beyond omics: From descriptive profiling to causal and scalable design of fermentation microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Fermentation microbiomes play essential roles in food production, feed preservation, waste valorization, and diverse sustainable industrial processes. Although multi-omics and systems biology have substantially advanced our understanding of their assembly, interactions, and functional dynamics, industrial translation remains constrained by fragmented datasets, limited causal validation, and transport constraints during scale-up. Large language models act as upper-level knowledge and workflow orchestrators, accelerating data integration, hybrid AI-mechanistic modeling, hypothesis generation, an
papers.summary: This review discusses how fermentation microbiomes can be understood and engineered beyond descriptive omics, emphasizing the need for causal validation and scalable design. It highlights the role of large language models as orchestrators for data integration and hybrid AI-mechanistic modeling to accelerate translation from lab to industry.

papers.title: Determinants influencing triage system at tertiary care centre as perceived by triage nurse: a qualitative study.
papers.abstract: The objective of this study is to explore the lived experiences of triage nurses.
papers.summary: This qualitative study explores the lived experiences of triage nurses at a tertiary care center to identify factors that influence the triage system. The findings highlight key determinants such as resource availability, communication challenges, and nurse workload, which can inform improvements in triage processes and patient care.

papers.title: HIT-MAP: A scalable approach to multimodal mapping of subcellular organization.
papers.abstract: Multimodal mapping of subcellular protein organization through imaging and interaction proteomics has been mostly confined to large consortia, owing to high per-target costs, reliance on target-specific antibodies or libraries of epitope-tagged cDNAs, and the lack of unified pipelines for coordinated data acquisition. Here, we present HIT-MAP (high-throughput integrated tagging for cell mapping), an end-to-end framework that couples endogenous epitope tagging with optimized wide-field immunofluorescence imaging and affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS). Applied to a pilot set of 16 r
papers.summary: HIT-MAP is a scalable, end-to-end framework that combines endogenous epitope tagging with optimized immunofluorescence imaging and affinity purification-mass spectrometry to enable multimodal mapping of subcellular protein organization. It reduces per-target costs and reliance on antibodies or cDNA libraries, making such mapping accessible beyond large consortia. The approach was demonstrated on a pilot set of 16 proteins, showing its feasibility for broader applications.

papers.title: Diabetic Hyperglycemia Induces Region-Specific Transcriptomic Remodeling in the Cochlea.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is associated with sensorineural hearing loss, but the cochlear molecular alterations related to this complication remain unclear. This pilot study aimed to characterize auditory function and region-specific transcriptomic changes in the diabetic cochlea.
papers.summary: This pilot study investigates how diabetic hyperglycemia affects hearing by examining region-specific gene expression changes in the cochlea. The findings reveal distinct transcriptomic remodeling across cochlear regions, providing initial molecular insights into diabetes-related sensorineural hearing loss.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics imputation and embedding with SpaMIE.
papers.abstract: SpaMIE is a deep graph neural network framework designed to tackle the challenge of multi-section integration in spatial multi-omics (SMO) datasets with systematic missing modalities. Current SMO platforms face limitations such as high cost and limited throughput, leading to many large-scale spatial atlases relying on cost-effective mono-omics measurements while only a few sections are profiled with full multi-omics technologies. This results in heterogeneous modality coverage across tissue sections. SpaMIE offers a two-stage solution. In the first stage, it performs spatially informed cross-m
papers.summary: SpaMIE is a deep graph neural network framework that integrates spatial multi-omics data across tissue sections with missing modalities, using a two-stage approach for imputation and embedding. It addresses the challenge of heterogeneous modality coverage in large-scale spatial atlases, enabling more comprehensive analysis of cost-effective mono-omics datasets.

papers.title: AMIUgraph: analysis and modeling of interactions for utility-driven benchmarking of graph-based models in healthcare.
papers.abstract: Graph-based machine learning approaches, including Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE) methods and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), have emerged as powerful tools for modeling complex biomedical data. However, a systematic and clinically grounded comparison of these approaches across heterogeneous healthcare graphs, accounting for both predictive performance and real-world deployment constraints, is still lacking.
papers.journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
papers.summary: This paper introduces AMIUgraph, a framework for benchmarking graph-based machine learning models (KGEs and GNNs) in healthcare. It provides a systematic, clinically grounded comparison across heterogeneous healthcare graphs, considering both predictive performance and real-world deployment constraints.

papers.title: ViBioChain: a blockchain-enabled architecture for privacy-preserving, ethically governed, and explainable personalized gene editing.
papers.abstract: Personalized gene editing demands robust mechanisms for privacy, ethical governance, and verifiable data integrity. This paper proposes ViBioChain, a modular blockchain-anchored architecture integrating five components: (1) differential chain-of-custody audit combining quantum fingerprinting with post-quantum signatures for immutable genomic audit trails; (2) proof-of-bioethical-compliance employing zero-knowledge proofs and AI-based ontology evaluation for automated bioethical gating; (3) federated genomic trust mesh (FGTM) enabling privacy-preserving collaborative model training with Renyi d
papers.summary: ViBioChain is a proposed blockchain-based architecture designed to address privacy, ethical governance, and data integrity in personalized gene editing. It integrates components like quantum fingerprinting for audit trails, zero-knowledge proofs for bioethical compliance, and federated learning for privacy-preserving model training, aiming to create a secure and transparent framework for genomic data management.

papers.title: LivestockDev: A multi-omics resource for exploring cross-species comparison of livestock embryogenesis.
papers.abstract: Advances in experimental and sequencing technologies have driven a surge in multi-omics data on early embryonic development in livestock species. Nevertheless, the absence of systematic data curation and standardized analytical frameworks has hindered research on early embryogenesis in livestock, limiting data integration, cross-species comparisons, and mechanistic insights. Here, we developed LivestockDev, an integrative multi-omics database dedicated to livestock embryogenesis. LivestockDev covers five major livestock species (cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, and horses) and systematically integr
papers.summary: LivestockDev is a new multi-omics database that integrates and standardizes early embryonic development data across five major livestock species (cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, and horses). It provides a centralized resource for cross-species comparisons and mechanistic studies, addressing the lack of systematic data curation in livestock embryogenesis.

papers.title: Mapping ovarian cellular and molecular landscape across the lifespan of women: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: With growing interest in ART, fertility preservation, and postmenopausal health of women, reproductive medicine is increasingly focused on characterizing oocytes and ovarian tissue composition, as well as understanding the molecular mechanisms that guide ovarian function throughout its lifecycle. High-throughput omics technologies have enabled the characterization of different molecular layers, leading to substantial advances in our understanding of their complex dynamics. However, not all molecular aspects are studied equally, and studies examining the same modalities often show inconsistenci
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the cellular and molecular landscape of the human ovary across the female lifespan, highlighting advances from high-throughput omics technologies while noting inconsistencies and gaps in the field. It underscores the need for more integrated and standardized approaches to fully understand ovarian function and its implications for fertility and postmenopausal health.

papers.title: FAIR Data Standards for AI in Plant Biology: Current Practice and Case Studies.
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a central analytical approach in plant science, supporting prediction, pattern discovery, and integration across molecular, phenotypic, and environmental data. While methodological advances have been rapid, progress is increasingly constrained less by algorithms than by the structure, semantics, and interoperability of the underlying data. In this review, we examine how the Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) principles are currently realized in AI-driven plant research and how different implementations shape which AI analyses are fe
papers.summary: This review examines how FAIR data principles are currently applied in AI-driven plant research, arguing that data structure and interoperability—not algorithms—are now the main bottleneck. It provides case studies showing how different FAIR implementations shape which AI analyses are feasible, and offers guidance for improving data practices.

papers.title: Ontology-driven energy-efficient SAID framework for 5G and IoT networks using cryptographic techniques.
papers.abstract: The rapid deployment and usage of 5G and IoT networks in smart cities present significant challenges for cybersecurity, particularly regarding energy efficiency and attack detection. Existing intrusion detection systems often fail to balance high detection accuracy with low energy consumption, especially in resource-constrained environments. This research paper proposes an ontology-driven novel computational framework for energy-efficient Security Attack Identification and Detection (SAID) in 5G and IoT networks. The research framework proposed is a combination of cryptographic algorithms and
papers.summary: This paper proposes an ontology-driven framework for energy-efficient security attack identification and detection (SAID) in 5G and IoT networks, combining cryptographic algorithms to balance detection accuracy with low energy consumption. The framework addresses the challenge of maintaining cybersecurity in resource-constrained smart city environments.

papers.title: Reproducible-by-design: Romics Processor, a FAIR ecosystem for multi-omics and spatial-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: Multi-omics and spatial-omics technologies are exploding in use, producing increasingly complex datasets. Existing bioinformatics tools are developing rapidly but fail to fully enforce the FAIR principles, leaving the field vulnerable to escalating issues in computational reproducibility. Here, we introduce a reproducible-by-design paradigm represented in an omics data processing package, RomicsProcessor. At its core, the "Romics_object", which is a self-contained digital artifact that encapsulates the full history of the data from the original data to the fully processed state, capturing the
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This paper introduces RomicsProcessor, a new bioinformatics package designed to enforce FAIR principles and reproducibility in multi-omics and spatial-omics data analysis. The core innovation is the 'Romics_object', a self-contained digital artifact that records the entire data processing history, from raw data to final results, ensuring that analyses are reproducible by design.

papers.title: Bioinformatics analysis identifies a novel 4-gene signature associated with immune cell infiltration in osteoarthritis: a combined bioinformatics and experimental validation study.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis is the most common degenerative joint condition, yet its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. This study aims to identify key differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in osteoarthritis-affected synovial tissues and investigate potential underlying immune mechanisms using bioinformatics approaches. Gene expression datasets GSE12021, GSE55235, and GSE55457 from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were analyzed, comprising 30 osteoarthritis and 28 normal synovial tissue samples. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using the limma R package. Functional enrichme
papers.summary: This study analyzed gene expression data from osteoarthritis synovial tissues to identify a novel 4-gene signature associated with immune cell infiltration. The findings suggest these genes may play a role in the immune mechanisms underlying osteoarthritis, providing potential biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

papers.title: VITAGRAPH: building a knowledge graph for biologically relevant learning tasks.
papers.abstract: The complexity of human biology poses ongoing challenges, driving global interdisciplinary research. Artificial intelligence has become a powerful tool in computational biology, where graph data structures model entities like protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks and gene functional networks. These networks support crucial tasks in network medicine, including gene-disease association prediction, drug repurposing, and polypharmacy side-effect analysis. Reliable machine learning predictions require high-quality data. We present VITAGRAPH, a comprehensive multi-purpose biological knowledge g
papers.summary: VITAGRAPH is a new comprehensive biological knowledge graph that integrates diverse biomedical data to support machine learning tasks such as gene-disease association prediction, drug repurposing, and polypharmacy side-effect analysis. It provides a high-quality, multi-purpose resource designed to improve the reliability of AI-driven predictions in network medicine.

papers.title: Advancing cross-domain integration and semantic technologies: proceedings of the 19th international symposium on integrative bioinformatics.
papers.abstract: This special issue of the Journal of Integrative Bioinformatics presents proceedings from the 19th International Symposium on Integrative Bioinformatics, which was held 10-12 September 2025. The featured contributions address critical bottlenecks in life science data management, specifically focusing on the practical implementation of FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) principles as an essential prerequisite for data integration and data interoperability. Comprising nine peer-reviewed articles, the issue highlights methodological advancements in cross-omics integration, s
papers.summary: This special issue presents proceedings from the 19th International Symposium on Integrative Bioinformatics, focusing on practical implementation of FAIR principles to improve data integration and interoperability in life sciences. The nine peer-reviewed articles highlight methodological advances in cross-omics integration and related areas.

papers.title: Integrating short-read and long-read single-cell transcriptomics of pig pituitary reveals mechanisms of high-altitude hypoxia adaptation.
papers.abstract: Acting as the central endocrine hub, the pituitary gland is closely related to the mechanism of adaptation to high-altitude hypoxia. Here, by integratively combining long-read (Oxford Nanopore) and short-read (Illumina) single-cell sequencing approaches, we profiled pituitaries from Diqing Tibetan pigs, inhabiting high-altitude environments (3,200 m) and Diannan small-ear pigs from low-altitude regions (500 m), thereby generating a full-length single-cell atlas, which in turn enabled the identification of molecular mechanisms potentially underlying adaptation to high-altitude hypoxia stress. S
papers.summary: This study integrates long-read and short-read single-cell transcriptomics to profile pituitary glands from high-altitude Tibetan pigs and low-altitude pigs, generating a full-length single-cell atlas. The analysis reveals molecular mechanisms, including cell-type-specific gene expression and isoform usage, that may underlie adaptation to high-altitude hypoxia stress.

papers.title: A haplotype-resolved, chromosome-scale genome assembly and annotation for Carya glabra (pignut hickory; Juglandaceae).
papers.abstract: Carya glabra (2n = 4x = 64), also known as pignut hickory, is a widely distributed species in the walnut family (Juglandaceae). Native to the central and eastern United States and southeastern Canada, C. glabra plays an important ecological role as a common upland forest species; it is closely related to several economically valuable nut trees, including Carya illinoinensis (pecan). A deeper understanding of the genetics of C. glabra is essential for studying its evolutionary history and biology, with potential implications for agricultural improvement of pecan. Here, we present the first nucl
papers.summary: This study presents the first haplotype-resolved, chromosome-scale genome assembly and annotation for Carya glabra (pignut hickory), a tetraploid species in the walnut family. The genome resource will facilitate evolutionary studies and potentially aid in agricultural improvement of related nut trees like pecan.

papers.title: Association of IL-8 and IL-18 Expression With Histone-Associated NETosis in Aqueous-Deficient and Evaporative Dry Eye Disease.
papers.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the ocular surface; however, upstream immune mechanisms contributing to DED are complex and unclear. This study aimed to identify differentially expressed tear proteins in patients with DED and elucidate the underlying disease mechanism.
papers.summary: This study identifies differentially expressed tear proteins in dry eye disease (DED) patients, specifically linking elevated IL-8 and IL-18 expression with histone-associated NETosis (a form of neutrophil cell death) in both aqueous-deficient and evaporative DED subtypes. The findings suggest that NETosis-related inflammatory pathways may be key upstream immune mechanisms contributing to DED pathology.

papers.title: PathMED: an R toolkit for single-sample molecular scoring and machine learning with omics data.
papers.abstract: Molecular scoring is a popular approach for studying pathway-level functional alterations with omics data. Using molecular scores for tasks such as single-sample molecular characterisation, phenotype prediction or disease stratification has several advantages compared to using omics data directly. Molecular scores provide biological interpretability and are more generalisable across datasets, facilitating data integration and machine learning applications. However, numerous scoring methods are available through different software packages, and currently there is a lack of tools to easily use t
papers.summary: PathMED is a new R toolkit that simplifies single-sample molecular scoring and machine learning with omics data, addressing the lack of integrated tools for this purpose. It provides a unified interface for multiple scoring methods and downstream ML tasks, enhancing interpretability and cross-dataset generalizability.

papers.title: IP-LC-MS/MS-Based Identification of Candidate TPL2 (MAP3K8)-Associated Proteins in Porcine PK-15 Cells.
papers.abstract: Tumor progression locus 2 (TPL2, also known as MAP-3K8/COT) is a kinase that regulates MAPK and NF-κB signaling and contributes to antiviral immunity. While mammalian TPL2 has been widely studied, the TPL2-associated protein profile in swine cells remains largely unexplored. In this study, we generated an IP-LC-MS/MS-based candidate dataset of TPL2-associated proteins in porcine kidney epithelial (PK-15) cells. FLAG-tagged TPL2 was overexpressed in PK-15 cells and enriched by immunoprecipitation, followed by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) analysis. After subtraction
papers.summary: This study used immunoprecipitation coupled with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (IP-LC-MS/MS) to identify candidate proteins associated with TPL2 (MAP3K8) in porcine PK-15 cells, providing the first dataset of TPL2-interacting proteins in swine. The findings lay groundwork for understanding TPL2's regulatory roles in porcine antiviral immunity and MAPK/NF-κB signaling.

papers.title: Nigericin-Triggered Phosphodynamics in Inflammasome Formation and Pyroptosis.
papers.abstract: Innate immune signaling relies heavily on phosphorylation cascades to mount effective immune responses. Although traditional innate immune signaling cascades following TLR4 stimulation have been investigated through a temporally quantitative phosphoproteomic lens, far fewer studies have applied these methods to distinct signaling following the inflammasome trigger leading to IL-1β release. Here, we conducted time-resolved phosphoproteomic profiling to investigate kinase signaling downstream of the inflammasome trigger nigericin. We found that nigericin induces rapid and potent alterations in t
papers.summary: This study uses time-resolved phosphoproteomics to map kinase signaling downstream of the inflammasome trigger nigericin, revealing rapid and potent phosphorylation changes that drive inflammasome formation and pyroptosis. It provides a new resource for understanding innate immune signaling beyond TLR4 pathways.

papers.title: Targeting Spatiotemporal Heterogeneity of oncomiRNAs: A New Frontier in Cancer Therapy.
papers.abstract: miRNAs are short RNA transcripts that modulate gene expression after transcription and have emerged as pivotal regulators of cancer biology. A subset, termed oncomiRNAs, functions as oncogenes or tumor suppressors, influencing key cellular events such as cell growth, programmed cell death, neovascularization, tissue invasion, and metastatic spread. Dysregulation of these miRNAs drives tumor initiation and progression, underscoring their role in cancer evolution. Traditionally, studies have relied on bulk tissue analyses, overlooking the profound spatiotemporal heterogeneity of oncomiRNA expres
papers.summary: This review discusses the role of oncomiRNAs in cancer and highlights the importance of their spatiotemporal heterogeneity, which is often missed by bulk tissue analyses. It proposes that targeting this heterogeneity represents a new frontier in cancer therapy.

papers.title: Integrated Network Analysis Suggests an miR-21/MMP/VEGF-Associated Regulatory Axis in Gastric Cancer.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) pathogenesis involves complex molecular interactions that remain incompletely understood at a biological systems level. While microRNA-21 (miR-21), matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) have been individually implicated in GC, their integrated role as a coordinated regulatory network remains uncharacterized. And we aim to reveal novel biology systems level insights into the miR-21/MMP/VEGF regulatory axis.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated network analysis to characterize a coordinated regulatory axis involving miR-21, matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) in gastric cancer, providing systems-level insights into their combined role in tumor progression. The findings suggest that these molecules function as an interconnected network rather than acting independently, potentially informing future therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Circulating multi-omic signature of disease severity and cholangiocarcinoma in primary sclerosing cholangitis.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease often associated with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) that can progress to cirrhosis or cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), both carrying a poor prognosis. The mechanisms driving disease progression remain poorly understood. We aimed to identify circulating multi-omic signatures linked to PSC severity (alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, fibrosis), IBD, and CCA to elucidate underlying biology and discover potential biomarkers for risk stratification and disease monitoring.
papers.summary: This study identifies circulating multi-omic signatures associated with disease severity, inflammatory bowel disease, and cholangiocarcinoma in primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), a chronic liver disease. The findings reveal potential biomarkers for risk stratification and monitoring, and provide insights into the biological mechanisms driving PSC progression.

papers.title: From parasite biology to predictive metabolic models.
papers.abstract: Protist parasites cause devastating diseases worldwide, yet their complex metabolism remains poorly understood. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) have emerged as powerful tools to systematically represent and simulate parasite metabolism, enabling the prediction of gene essentiality, metabolic vulnerabilities, and host-parasite interactions. This review examines the current landscape of GEMs for protist pathogens, focusing on the key modeling decisions (objective functions, constraints, and compartmentalization) that govern model behavior and predictive scope. We discuss how these choices s
papers.summary: This review discusses how genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) are used to study the metabolism of protist parasites, which cause major diseases. It highlights key modeling decisions—such as objective functions, constraints, and compartmentalization—that influence the models' ability to predict gene essentiality and host-parasite interactions. The paper serves as a guide for researchers looking to apply or improve GEMs in parasitology.

papers.title: De novo whole transcriptome sequencing reveals differentially expressed messenger RNA and MicroRNA in hepatopancreas of Pandalus hypsinotus.
papers.abstract: Pandalus hypsinotus (P. hypsinotus), also known as coonstripe shrimp, has high economic value and is widely distributed in Alaska, the Bering Sea and the East Sea of Korea. However, owing to the low catch rates and patchy spatial distribution, transcriptome-based studies on this species remain limited. Transcriptome analyses using PacBio Iso-Seq and Illumina RNA sequencing techniques were performed to establish a de novo unigene set of P. hypsinotus and identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the hepatopancreas compared to the tail muscle. A search of all the unigenes against Gene On
papers.summary: This study provides the first de novo whole transcriptome assembly for the coonstripe shrimp (Pandalus hypsinotus) using PacBio Iso-Seq and Illumina RNA-seq, identifying differentially expressed mRNAs and microRNAs in the hepatopancreas compared to tail muscle. The findings offer a valuable genomic resource for this economically important species and shed light on tissue-specific gene expression.

papers.title: Leveraging expression quantitative trait loci information in single-cell resolution to identify cell-specific genes for Basal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC), the most common skin cancer, is driven by UV-induced DNA damage and shaped by immune surveillance. Although GWAS has identified over 140 risk loci, their cell-type-specific effects remain obscured by tissue-level averaging.
papers.summary: This study integrates expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) data with single-cell RNA sequencing to identify cell-type-specific genes associated with basal cell carcinoma (BCC) risk, overcoming the limitations of tissue-level averaging in GWAS. The approach reveals immune and stromal cell-specific gene expression patterns that may clarify the cellular mechanisms underlying BCC susceptibility.

papers.title: Editorial: Big data in systems biology.
papers.summary: This editorial introduces a Research Topic on big data in systems biology, highlighting the challenges and opportunities of integrating large-scale omics datasets to understand complex biological systems. It emphasizes the need for new computational and statistical methods to handle data heterogeneity and scale.
